interpretation: Reading B (universal), first half: 'every object of thought (πᾶν τὸ διανοητὸν καὶ νοητὸν), thought either affirms or denies' is read as a claim about every object of thought, and every proposition is taken as a possible object of thought. It says that each proposition is the object of some affirmation or denial, not yet that this thought is true or false. The extension from 'every object of thought' to every proposition is the reading's own step.
